Cross-paradigm analysis using RaMP multi-DB ORA and mummichog m/z-direct enrichment converges on the 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 / MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as the overwhelming top hit, with FDR below 1e-17 in ORA and 100% compound overlap (14/14) in mummichog. react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set is dominated by six C19-steroid hormones and their immediate precursors. Cross-paradigm analysis using RaMP multi-DB ORA and mummichog m/z-direct enrichment converges on the 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway (SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 / MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as the overwhelming top hit, with FDR below 1e-17 in ORA and 100% compound overlap (14/14) in mummichog. The six driver steroids — testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, dihydrotestosterone, 17β-estradiol, and estrone — are substrate and product intermediates of CYP17A1, CYP19A1 (aromatase), HSD17B, and AKR1C family enzymes. Their coordinated perturbation strongly implicates altered steroidogenic flux, consistent with disruption of the 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' Reactome module (R-HSA-196071, FDR = 4.38e-17) and 'Estrogen biosynthesis' (R-HSA-193144). The outlier metabolite 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043) independently maps to 'Tyrosine metabolism' (MUMM:rank 2, p = 0.023), suggesting a secondary catecholamine-shunt effect. Warfarin (C01541) does not map to any steroid pathway in the ORA or KEGG libraries and appears only in the mummichog empirical network, likely reflecting SMILES-based mass similarity rather than true biological membership. The convergence of six structurally resolved steroids on a single, highly significant pathway across three independent computational paradigms provides a robust biological signature of altered sex-steroid homeostasis under the treatment condition.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Metabolomics analysis of eight differential metabolites revealed convergent evidence across three independent paradigms for disrupted sex-steroid homeostasis. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00068, KEGG:map00150) and the related Aromatase deficiency context (SMPDB:SMP00565) as top hits with FDR=4.97e-18, implicating six steroid compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment independently returned Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism as its rank-0 pathway (p=8.4e-5) with complete overlap of the six driver steroids, and Tyrosine metabolism as a secondary signal via 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (p=0.028). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA reported KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as its top hit (p=5.77e-7), hitting the same six steroids. The convergence of these orthogonal methods on the androgen-estrogen metabolic grid constitutes a high-confidence biological finding. The secondary tyrosine metabolism signal warrants mechanistic follow-up given the known pharmacological interaction between warfarin and aromatic amine metabolism.
